title: sluis overview - $cluster
description: The token service and its controllers: the issuer's requests, errors and latency, tokens and sign-ins, signing keys, the controllers' ticks and leases, the storage ports, and GitHub rate limits and seats.

panels.title: Signing keys published
panels.description: Keys in the JWKS, the lowest across algorithms and replicas. Healthy is at least one. Zero is an issuer nobody can verify a token against: see SluisNoSigningKeyPublished in the telemetry runbook.

panels.title: 5xx share (1h)
panels.description: The share of the issuer's requests answered 5xx. Healthy is zero: its refusals are 4xx. The request panels below name the route.

panels.title: Sign-in failures (1h)
panels.description: Sign-ins that did not complete. A few are people closing a tab; a climb in one reason is the signal. The reasons are in the sign-in panel below.

panels.title: Reuse detected (1h)
panels.description: A spent authorization code or refresh token presented again. A code reuse also ends the session it opened. A refresh token outside the grace window is spent or unknown (the two are not told apart). A burst is a client bug or a stolen credential.

panels.title: Targets not ticking
panels.description: Live targets (GitHub organisations, Slack workspaces, Outline workspaces: a tick counted in the last 15 minutes) with no ok tick in the last hour, four default intervals, from the tick counter. See SluisTickStale.

targets.expr: count(max by (k8s_cluster_name, namespace, kind, target) (last_over_time(sluis_ticks_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace"}[15m])) unless sum by (k8s_cluster_name, namespace, kind, target) (increase(sluis_ticks_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",outcome="ok"}[1h])) > 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Port errors (1h)
panels.description: Storage port calls that ended unavailable or error. Not counted: a lost compare-and-swap, a create over a live key, a missing key. Healthy is zero.

panels.title: Requests per second, by route
panels.description: What the issuer's listener answers, by route (a fixed set of names, never the raw path). token and authorize are the protocol; login_* the sign-in pages; console_* the console.

panels.title: 5xx per second, by route
panels.description: Requests answered with a server error. Should be a flat zero; compare with the request rate above.

panels.title: Latency p99, by route
panels.description: The 99th-percentile time the listener took, by route. The token endpoint is one store write and a signature: milliseconds.

panels.title: Token endpoint latency, p50 and p99, and Cloudflare mints
panels.description: The token endpoint on its own, the one clients wait on. SluisTokenEndpointSlow fires on its p99. A Cloudflare credential mint (route token_mint) is apart: it waits on the Cloudflare module and on Cloudflare, so seconds are its normal; its p95 is over an hour, as mints are few. SluisTokenMintSlow fires on it.

panels.title: Tokens issued per second, by client
panels.description: Access tokens signed, by the client id the policy declares (anything it does not declare is `other`, a workload's exchange is `none`).

panels.title: Tokens issued per second, by grant
panels.description: The same tokens by grant type: authorization_code (a sign-in), refresh_token, token_exchange (a workload or a person trading a token), client_credentials, console_mint (the console reading another service as the person).

panels.title: Sign-in failures per second, by reason
panels.description: Why sign-ins did not complete: bad_state (a stale or foreign callback), provider_failed (the directory's own exchange), directory_refused, directory_unreachable, not_entitled, recovery_refused, unaudited, not_waiting, unknown_provider, bad_request.

panels.title: Sign-ins completed per second, by method
panels.description: Sign-ins that completed, by how the person was proved: a directory's kind, recovery, or an existing browser session.

panels.title: Reuse detected, by kind
panels.description: A spent authorization code or refresh token presented again. Should be a flat zero.

panels.title: Signing keys: published and age of the active key
panels.description: Keys in the JWKS by algorithm (left) and the age of the active key (the second series, in seconds). A healthy key is at most about 335 days old with the chart's defaults; SluisSigningKeyRotationStalled fires past 350.

panels.title: Ticks per second, by kind and outcome
panels.description: Ticks of the GitHub and Slack controllers. failed is a report that says failed or a tick that returned an error; ok includes in-sync, applied, held and dry-run.

panels.title: Tick duration p99, by kind
panels.description: How long a tick of a target takes. A climb is a slow GitHub or Slack, a console under load, or a large organisation.

panels.title: Ok ticks in the last hour, by target
panels.description: For every target, its ok ticks over the last hour, from the tick counter: four at the default interval (15m). A line at zero for a target that still reports is a target nobody is reconciling: SluisTickStale.

panels.title: Failed ticks, by target
panels.description: Failed ticks per target over the interval. SluisTickFailing fires on three in 45 minutes.

panels.title: Leases held, by kind
panels.description: Tick leases this runner holds now. One per target being ticked; a controller with several replicas shows each replica's own.

panels.title: Leases acquired, contended and lost, per second
panels.description: Acquired: taken. Contended: asked for and another runner held it (the normal answer of the replica that did not win). Lost: held and then taken over or not renewable; repeated is SluisLeaseLost.

panels.title: Port calls per second, by port and outcome
panels.description: Calls to the state, index and blob ports. conflict is a lost compare-and-swap (a lease or a session rotation working), exists a create over a live key, not_found a missing key; unavailable and error are the store failing.

panels.title: Port failures, share of calls by port
panels.description: The share of calls that ended unavailable or error. SluisPortErrors fires on 5% over five minutes.

panels.title: Port latency p99, by port and operation
panels.description: The 99th-percentile time of a port call. The legacy adapter is Valkey and the namespace's ConfigMaps and Secrets: a blob write is an API server round trip, a state call one Valkey command.

panels.title: Compare-and-swap conflicts per second, by operation
panels.description: Writes that lost a race: update, delete_if_revision and write_if_version answering conflict. A trickle is replicas sharing a lease or rotating a session; a sustained rate is two things fighting.

panels.title: AWS SDK call errors per second, by service and exception
panels.description: Calls to AWS (DynamoDB, SSM, SQS, S3, Lambda) that returned an error, from the SDK's own client.call.errors counter, for the sluis services of the cluster. Several errors are ordinary outcomes of a conditional write or a probe and are expected at a steady rate: ConditionalCheckFailedException (a lost compare-and-swap), NotFound, PreconditionFailed and ParameterNotFound (a read of something not yet stored). Look for a rate that moves, for *http.ResponseError (AWS answered with a failure) and for context.deadlineExceededError (a call that outlived its deadline); the next panel leaves the expected ones out.

panels.title: AWS SDK call failure share, by service
panels.description: Share of the calls to each AWS service that failed in a way that is not an ordinary conditional outcome (ConditionalCheckFailedException, NotFound, PreconditionFailed and ParameterNotFound are left out), from client.call.errors over client.call.duration. A service above a few percent for a quarter of an hour is a dependency to look at: the Storage ports row shows whether the store is the one. A service that made calls and had no failure reads 0.

targets.expr: (sum by (rpc_service) (rate(client_call_errors_total{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~".*sluis.*",exception_type!~"NotFound|PreconditionFailed|ParameterNotFound|ConditionalCheckFailedException"}[$__rate_interval])) or 0 * sum by (rpc_service) (rate(client_call_duration_seconds_count{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~".*sluis.*"}[$__rate_interval]))) / sum by (rpc_service) (rate(client_call_duration_seconds_count{k8s_cluster_name=~"$cluster",namespace=~"$namespace",job=~".*sluis.*"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Rate limit remaining, by resource
panels.description: Requests left in GitHub's budget as last reported on a response. SluisGitHubRateLimitLow fires under 100 for 30 minutes.

panels.title: Rate-limit waits per second, by kind
panels.description: Waits for a GitHub rate limit, by kind: retry_after (GitHub named a time), primary (the budget was spent; waited for its reset) or secondary (an abuse limit, waited a minute). Each kind reads 0 once the controllers have made a call, so a flat line is a quiet day and "no data" is a controller that has not called GitHub.

panels.title: Seats short, by organisation
panels.description: Invitations the last pass could not send for want of a free seat. Healthy is zero: SluisSeatsShort.

panels.title: Seats free, by organisation
panels.description: Free seats as last read; absent while the seats cannot be read.
